newsitem.title: USA: Mich. voters approve $370.3 mln of school bonds.
newsitem.headline: Mich. voters approve $370.3 mln of school bonds.

text.p: Voters in north suburban Detroit communities approved major referendums totalling $370.3 million of bonds for school projects, including one for $100.575 million that passed by five votes, school officials said Tuesday.

Residents of the Rochester Community Schools district voted 6,982 to 6,977 to approve a general obligation bond issuance to build a new high school and renovate two others, said Michael Dixon, assistant superintendent for business.
Rochester voters rejected referendums for $8.41 million of bonds to fund technological improvements for grade schools and $2.585 million to build an operation services facility, Dixon said.

Dixon said Thrun, Maatsch & Nordberg of Lansing will serve as bond counsel and Erickson & Associates Ltd of Lansing as financial adviser. School officials had hoped to get into the market by Aug. 1, but no date has been set, he added.
Voters in the Troy School District approved a $71.475 million bond referendum for capital and technological improvements, said Mike Adamczyk, executive director for business services.
Adamczyk said he wants to sell the general obligation bonds before Aug. 1 to begin equipment purchases for the district's fiscal year, which begins July 1.
Financial adviser for the deal will be Stauder, Barch & Associates Inc of Ann Arbor and Thrun, Maatsch will serve as bond counsel, Adamczyk said.

Clarkston Community Schools residents approved a referendum for $57.65 million of general obligation bonds for a new elementary school, renovation of five elementary school buildings and technological improvements, spokeswoman Barbara Johns said.
Johns said that Thrun, Maatsch has been selected as bond counsel and Stauder, Barch as financial adviser. They hope to get into the market the week of July 7, she said.
Residents of Northville Public Schools approved $61.5 million of bonds to build a new high school and add elementary school classrooms.
Residents of L'Anse Creuse approved $79.1 million of bonds for a number of construction and renovation projects.
Southgate residents rejected a $65.8 million bond referendum by a nearly three to one margin, district officials said.
